notes: §1985:VII.4.3.4 GR4: "An OPEN statement must be successfully executed prior to the execution of any of the permissible input-output statements.", and Table 2 permits READ in the input and I-O modes, WRITE in the output and extend modes and REWRITE in the I-O mode. Each statement's runtime entry tests the connector's open mode first: ReadRecord asks SequentialReadGuard, whose ReadOpenModeGuard answers 47 unless the file is open INPUT or I-O; Write and WriteAdvancing answer 48 unless it is open OUTPUT or EXTEND; RewriteRecord asks MutationOpenModeGuard, which answers 49 unless it is open I-O. A file is open only from a successful OPEN to its CLOSE, so the same statuses answer a statement on a file never opened, opened unsuccessfully or closed (§1985:VII.1.3.5: "The execution of a READ statement is attempted on a file not open in the input or I-O mode.", and the WRITE and REWRITE values 48 and 49). The guards have no edition arm; what the 1985 edition needs is that the table holds no fourth statement, and the START a later edition adds for a sequential file is refused at 85 (BindStart: COBOL0862 for START with no FIRST or LAST; VisitStartStatement: COBOL0900 for START FIRST and START LAST), as is DELETE (COBOL0865). Probed at --std 85 beside the witness's cells: READ INTO, WRITE FROM and WRITE with BEFORE or AFTER ADVANCING take the cells of the plain statements (WRITE ADVANCING is 48 in the input and I-O modes and 00 in the extend mode; READ INTO is 47 and WRITE FROM ADVANCING 48 on a file not open); REWRITE is 49 in the output and extend modes and on a file not open; 47, 48 and 49 answer READ, WRITE and REWRITE on a file whose OPEN INPUT failed with 35 and on a file after CLOSE. The witness runs all twelve cells and the never-opened case with a USE procedure that counts the seven refusals, then reads the file back to show that only the permitted statements changed it.

next.reason: 1985 GR4: 'An OPEN statement must be successfully executed prior to the execution of any of the permissible input-output statements'; Table 2 permits for a sequential file only READ (input, I-O), WRITE (output, extend) and REWRITE (I-O). §2023:14.9.27.4 GR8 keeps the prior OPEN ('an OPEN statement shall previously be successfully executed') with GR6, and Table 20's sequential-access rows keep READ, WRITE, REWRITE as in 1985 (statuses 47-49: §2023:14.9.30.4 GR2, §2023:14.9.51.4 GR3, §2023:14.9.35.4 GR3). But Table 20 adds START (input, I-O) for sequential access, which a sequential file may now use ('If the organization of the file referenced by file-name-1 is sequential, either the FIRST or the LAST phrase shall be specified', §2023:14.9.41.3 SR2; status 23 when 'a START statement is attempted on a sequential file that has no records', §2023:9.1.13.5 GR3). 2023 accepts a statement the 1985 table did not permit: a case added.
